ai.description: *Takydromus khasiensis* is a slender lizard reaching 6 cm snout-vent length. It is olive-brown with a distinct white lateral stripe and possesses a very long, whip-like tail and four femoral pores.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Takydromus khasiensis* is best distinguished by the presence of only two pairs of chin shields, whereas most other Indian *Takydromus* species possess three or more pairs.
ai.habitat: *Takydromus khasiensis* inhabits the grassy hills and scrublands of the Khasi Hills in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Khasi grass lizard is primarily diurnal, utilizing its long, prehensile tail to navigate through tall grasses and shrubs while actively hunting for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Takydromus khasiensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Takydromus khasiensis* is endemic to Northeast India, primarily inhabiting the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
